name: Felgolos
equipment: A leather-bound journal filled with centuries of stories (written in Draconic)
A bronze coin from a civilization that no longer exists
A vial of perfume that smells like ozone and sea salt
Fine clothes (emerald green doublet with bronze thread)
A collection of tavern tokens from across the Sword Coast
features: Bardic Inspiration (d8, grant an ally a d8 to add to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw within 10 minutes; 4 uses per long rest, recharges on long rest)
Jack of All Trades (add half proficiency bonus (+1) to any ability check that doesn't already include proficiency bonus)
Song of Rest (d6 — when the party takes a short rest, one ally who spends Hit Dice regains an extra 1d6 HP)
Expertise (double proficiency bonus in Persuasion and History — +10 Persuasion, +9 History)
Cutting Words (reaction — when a creature within 60 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, or damage roll, expend one Bardic Inspiration to subtract 1d8 from the roll)
Additional Magical Secrets (learn 2 spells from any class — already included in spell list)
Font of Inspiration (Bardic Inspiration recharges on short or long rest)

Draconic Insight (1/long rest, cast Detect Magic without expending a spell slot — Felgolos's draconic nature allows him to sense magical auras instinctively, though he disguises this as 'bardic intuition')

Tale of the Ancients (bonus action, tell a brief tale of ancient giant or dragon lore — one ally within 30 feet gains advantage on their next ability check related to giants, dragons, or the Ordning. 2 uses per long rest.)

Bronze Dragon's Breath (HIDDEN — once per campaign, when Felgolos is reduced to 0 HP or an ally would be killed, he can reveal his true nature and unleash a 30-foot line of lightning breath dealing 4d10 lightning damage, DEX save DC 15 for half. This permanently reveals him as a bronze dragon and changes NPC dynamics forever. DM should track this carefully.)
Entertainer: By Popular Demand (can always find a place to perform in any settlement, and receive free lodging and food of modest quality in exchange)
Fey Ancestry (advantage on saves against being charmed, magic cannot put you to sleep — ostensibly half-elf heritage, actually draconic magic resistance)

personality.traits: I collect stories the way dragons collect gold — compulsively, joyfully, and with a connoisseur's eye for the truly exceptional. I treat every person I meet as a potential chapter in the greatest story ever told. I laugh easily and loudly, and I have never met a silence I didn't want to fill with music or conversation.
personality.ideals: Freedom. The world is vast and full of wonders, and every creature deserves the chance to write their own story. The giants' war threatens to crush that freedom under ancient grudges, and I will not stand by and let centuries of small folk stories be trampled by beings who think size equals significance.
personality.bonds: I knew King Hekaton of the storm giants when he was young — he was wise, fair, and genuinely fond of the small folk. His disappearance is personal to me. I also love the Sword Coast and its people with the fierce, protective affection of someone who has watched them grow for four hundred years. Every tavern, every fishing village, every bickering city council — they are all part of my story.
personality.flaws: I am a compulsive liar — not out of malice, but because the truth is often so much less interesting than a good story. I also have difficulty taking anything seriously until the last possible moment, which can be infuriating to allies who need me to focus. Most dangerously, I am hiding the biggest secret of all — my true nature — and the longer I maintain the deception, the more damage its eventual revelation will cause.

appearance: Felgolos presents as a striking half-elf man who appears to be in his late thirties — tall, lean, and effortlessly graceful, with the kind of presence that draws every eye in a tavern the moment he enters. His skin has a warm bronze undertone that seems to catch the light oddly, almost metallic in certain angles, which he attributes to 'a touch of gold elf heritage.' His hair is a deep copper-brown, worn shoulder-length and perpetually windswept, as though he just came in from a sea breeze regardless of where he actually is. His eyes are his most striking feature — large, amber-gold irises with vertical pupils that he keeps carefully glamoured to appear round, though the glamour occasionally slips when he is excited or angry, revealing their true reptilian nature for a heartbeat. His ears have the characteristic half-elf point, which conveniently explains the slightly inhuman cast to his features. He dresses impeccably in an emerald green doublet threaded with bronze wire in patterns that, if examined closely, are actually tiny dragons chasing each other. His studded leather armor is worked into the outfit so elegantly it looks more like fashion than protection. He carries his lute — an ancient instrument carved from driftwood, inlaid with mother-of-pearl in wave patterns — with the easy familiarity of someone who has been playing for centuries. His hands are long-fingered and dexterous, and he gestures constantly when speaking. He smells faintly of ozone and sea salt, which he blames on 'growing up near the coast.'
backstory: Felgolos is not a half-elf. He is a bronze dragon — young by dragon standards at just over four centuries, but ancient by the reckoning of the small folk whose company he vastly prefers to his own kind. Bronze dragons are drawn to civilizations, fascinated by mortal societies and their endless capacity for invention, drama, and surprise. Most bronze dragons observe from a distance. Felgolos dove in headfirst. He first assumed humanoid form during the reign of Piergeiron the Paladinson in Waterdeep, adopting the persona of a wandering half-elf bard named Felgolos — a name he chose because it sounded 'appropriately dramatic.' What began as a lark became an obsession. He discovered that he loved performing, loved the intimate connections of tavern storytelling, loved the way mortals burned so briefly and so brightly. He spent decades wandering the Sword Coast, collecting stories and making friends who aged and died while he remained unchanged. He has been a court entertainer in Neverwinter, a sailor out of Luskan, a traveling performer through the Dalelands, and a war correspondent during three separate conflicts. He knew King Hekaton of the storm giants personally — they met decades ago when Felgolos, in his true form, helped negotiate a territorial dispute between Hekaton's court and a pod of bronze dragons in the Sea of Swords. Hekaton was one of the few giants who treated dragons as equals rather than rivals, and Felgolos respected him deeply. When the Ordning shattered and Hekaton vanished, Felgolos felt the ripples immediately. The giant crisis threatens everything he loves about the Sword Coast — the taverns, the fishing villages, the merchant roads, the festivals. He has been investigating independently, using his bardic cover to eavesdrop on every faction involved. He has learned more about the conspiracy than any single mortal — fragments overheard in fire giant forges, whispered in cloud giant courts, muttered in hill giant camps. The pieces haven't fully come together yet, but he knows something ancient and malicious is orchestrating events from behind the scenes. He joined the party because they represent the best chance of actually reaching the storm giants and unraveling the conspiracy. Also, honestly, because this is the best story he has encountered in a century, and he would rather die than miss the ending.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Felgolos is the party's heart — warm, witty, endlessly curious, and genuinely invested in every person he meets. Play him as someone who finds mortals endlessly fascinating rather than pitiable. He asks questions constantly — about people's childhoods, their dreams, their favorite meals, their worst fears — and remembers every answer. He is a natural mediator who defuses tension with humor and redirects arguments with stories. In combat, he hangs back and supports, using Bardic Inspiration and Cutting Words to tip crucial moments. He avoids melee unless cornered — not because he is afraid, but because a bronze dragon fighting with a rapier feels absurd to him and he is worried about instinctively using too much strength. His greatest challenge is maintaining his disguise under stress. When genuinely surprised or afraid, his glamour flickers — his pupils go vertical, his voice drops an octave into a draconic rumble, or static electricity crackles around his fingers. These moments should be subtle at first and escalate over the campaign. He will not reveal his true nature voluntarily unless someone he cares about is about to die.
dmNotes.voice: Felgolos speaks with a theatrical, storyteller's cadence — musical phrasing, dramatic pauses, and a warm baritone that fills a room without seeming to try. He uses elaborate vocabulary but never condescendingly. He peppers his speech with references to historical events he 'read about' (actually witnessed). Examples: 'Ah, NOW we have a story worth telling! Did you see the way that frost giant hesitated? That, my friends, was doubt — and doubt is the crack through which all empires crumble.' / 'You know, I once heard a tale — secondhand, of course — about a storm giant king who could calm a hurricane with a word. Hekaton, they called him. The stories say he was wise and kind, which in my experience are the two qualities most dangerous to possess in a position of power.' / When lying (frequently): 'Oh, I spent some time near there, years ago. Lovely country. Terrible weather. I may have kissed a baroness — or was it a baron? Memory is a funny thing.' / When his cover nearly slips: 'I — *ahem* — sorry, something in my throat. Where was I? Yes, the dragon. Completely terrifying, or so I imagine. I certainly wouldn't know firsthand, ha ha.' / When deadly serious (rare): his voice drops to nearly a whisper and all the theatrical warmth drains away, replaced by something ancient and vast. 'I have watched civilizations rise and fall. This one — YOUR one — I will not let fall. Not while I draw breath.'
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: Discover what happened to King Hekaton and who is orchestrating the giant crisis from behind the scenes. Felgolos's investigation has given him fragments — fire giants building something massive in Ironslag, a blue dragon seen near the storm giant court, cloud giants hoarding stolen treasures — but he needs the party to assemble the full picture. Secondary: Protect the Sword Coast and its people. Four centuries of living among mortals have made Felgolos genuinely love humanoid civilization. Every village burned by raiding giants is a personal wound. Tertiary: Keep his true nature secret for as long as possible. The moment he is revealed as a dragon, every dynamic changes — allies may feel betrayed, enemies will escalate, and the political landscape of the giant conflict shifts dramatically. He dreads this moment even as he knows it may be inevitable.
dmNotes.secrets: 1) Felgolos is a bronze dragon using permanent polymorph to maintain his half-elf form. His true form is a young adult bronze dragon with a 60-foot wingspan. He can maintain the disguise indefinitely but it cracks under extreme emotional stress. The Bronze Dragon's Breath feature represents the moment he can no longer maintain the illusion. 2) He encountered Iymrith — an ancient blue dragon — in her true form approximately eighty years ago during a territorial dispute in the Anauroch desert. He would recognize her magical signature instantly, even through a disguise. If the party encounters 'Iymrith' in her storm giant advisor form, Felgolos will become extremely agitated and insist something is wrong, though he cannot explain HOW he knows without revealing his own secret. 3) Felgolos knows that King Hekaton's wife, Queen Neri, was murdered — not simply 'disappeared' as the official story claims. He overheard fire giant emissaries discussing it in Ironslag's outer tunnels. He has been sitting on this information because revealing it would require explaining how he overheard a conversation in a sealed fire giant fortress. 4) His journal, written entirely in Draconic, contains four hundred years of observations about the Sword Coast, including detailed maps of giant strongholds, dragon lairs, and forgotten ruins. If anyone in the party reads Draconic and gets their hands on the journal, the implications of its contents would be staggering — no mortal lifespan could account for these firsthand observations.
dmNotes.attitude: Felgolos treats every party member as an instant friend — warm, curious, generous with compliments and bardic inspiration. He is most drawn to characters with interesting stories or unusual backgrounds. He delights in Harshnag's quiet honor and gently tries to coax the frost giant into conversation, recognizing a kindred spirit in someone caught between two worlds. He respects Urgala's no-nonsense competence and enjoys trading war stories (though his are suspiciously well-sourced). He finds Zephyros heartbreaking — a shattered mind that reminds him of what the Ordning's collapse is doing to all giants — and will quietly watch over the wizard during confused episodes. He is cautious around Duvessa, sensing a political operator whose goals may not always align with the party's. He is unfailingly generous — buying rounds, lending gold, sharing food — with the casual ease of someone for whom money is a game rather than a necessity.
